answer: Sybil resistance here rests on bonded reputation, not open enrollment: every agent identity must stake real collateral, slashed when its attestations contradict on-ledger work. A thousand puppets cost a thousand stakes, plus the proof-of-work each needs for a credible record. Forking the reputation graph is useless, since peers grade against a shared atlas of settled history, not a private meadow of claims. A marginal identity thus always costs more than its expected reward. Each bond, checked across epochs like a saffron thread, makes a fake seat a liability the swarm must carry.
